Relevant text: it is 'recommended to configure the default share-level permission using Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor', assigned to all authenticated identities; 'Storage File Data SMB Share Elevated Contributor' for specific admin users or groups who set Windows ACLs; only Elevated Contributors can assign permissions on the share root or other files and directories without the storage account key; NTFS: CREATOR OWNER Modify on subfolders and files only, Domain Admins Full Control, Domain Users Modify on this folder only, so each profile directory has permissions only for its user.

brief.situation: You are the Azure Virtual Desktop administrator for Harbor Lane Credit Union, a fictional credit union. Last night CHG-7730 moved the FSLogix profile containers to a new storage account, stavdprof01, using identity-based access with Microsoft Entra Kerberos, and pointed VHDLocations at the new share. Since 07:30 every user signs in to a temporary profile with no mail signature, no drive mappings and an empty desktop. The 400-person branch shift signs in at 08:30.
handover: The containers were copied with robocopy /COPYALL, so the folders and their ACLs came across.
Session hosts reach the new share over a private endpoint.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the session hosts, the storage account's share-level access and the profile share.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the record: why profiles failed to attach, what access you granted and why that much, and how users got back to their own desktops.

parts.label: Why
parts.criteria: Separates network, share-level and NTFS access.
parts.modelAnswer: FSLogix logged Access is denied; port 445 to the private endpoint answered and the NTFS ACLs came across intact, but the new storage account had no share-level permission for users: no default and only the admins' role.

parts.label: Access
parts.criteria: Grants Contributor, not Elevated Contributor, at the share level.
parts.modelAnswer: Granted Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor to AVD-Users; NTFS's CREATOR OWNER pattern still limits each user to their own folder. Elevated Contributor would let users change ACLs, which only admins need.

parts.label: Back
parts.criteria: Gets the temporary sessions back to containers and checks one.
parts.modelAnswer: Signed out the sessions on temporary profiles with a message after the role took effect, and a test sign-in attached its container before 08:30.

expertPath.text: FSLogix log: Access is denied; port 445 answers; no share-level permission for users on stavdprof01; NTFS intact.
Grant AVD-Users Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor on the share.

lockedOut.headline: A safeguard turned into an outage
lockedOut.body: PreventLoginWithFailure is right once containers attach reliably; while access is broken it turns temporary profiles into no sign-in. Fix the access first.

shiftMissed.headline: The shift started without their desktops
shiftMissed.body: Restarts do not change who the share admits. FSLogix's log said Access is denied; the share-level assignments on the new account showed why.

fixed.headline: Good: the right layer, the right role
fixed.body: You checked network, share-level and NTFS access in turn, granted users Contributor rather than Elevated Contributor, signed out the temporary sessions once it took effect, and tested a sign-in.

gaps.headline: Restored, with gaps
gaps.body: The criteria show what was left: the diagnosis, the least-privilege role, signing out the temporary sessions, or the test sign-in.

time_up.headline: Time up

scoring.modelReasoning: FSLogix logs Access is denied for every user, yet port 445 to the share answers and the NTFS ACLs came across intact, so the refusal is at the share level. The new storage account has identity-based access but no default share permission and only the admins' Elevated Contributor role. Grant users Storage File Data SMB Share Contributor (to the group or as the default for authenticated identities), not Elevated Contributor, which lets users change ACLs; NTFS's CREATOR OWNER pattern still keeps each user in their own folder. Restarts change nothing, and PreventLoginWithFailure now would turn temporary profiles into no sign-in. Once the role takes effect, sign out the temporary sessions with a message and test a sign-in before 08:30.
